title: One-way functions from P ≠ NP
open: Determine whether worst-case hardness expressed by P ≠ NP alone implies the existence of one-way functions.
status: Open for decades. Worst-case-to-average-case reductions face substantial barriers; worst-case hardness is not presently interchangeable with cryptographic average-case hardness.
why: This would connect the central complexity-theoretic conjecture directly to cryptographic security.
key_works: Akavia, Goldreich, Goldwasser, and Moshkovitz, 2005, *On Basing One-Way Functions on NP-Hardness*.

title: Collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary one-way functions
open: Determine whether general one-way functions suffice for collision-resistant hash families through constructions not excluded by black-box lower bounds.
status: Longstanding. Known separations distinguish collision resistance from the hashing properties routinely obtained from one-way functions.
why: Collision resistance supports commitments, authenticated data structures, and many proof systems.
key_works: Simon, 1998, *Finding Collisions on a One-Way Street: Can Secure Hash Functions Be Based on General Assumptions?*; Couteau, Farshim, and Mahmoody, 2021, *Black-Box Uselessness: Composing Separations in Cryptography*, ePrint 2021/016.

title: Injective one-way functions from general one-way functions
open: Construct injective one-way functions from arbitrary, potentially highly many-to-one, one-way functions without assuming additional hardness.
status: Open. Injective constructions follow from particular number-theoretic assumptions, but that does not give a general transformation.
why: Injectivity simplifies commitments, authentication, and cryptographic reductions.
key_works: Goldreich, Levin, and Nisan, 1995, *On Constructing 1-1 One-Way Functions*, ECCC TR95-029.

title: One-way permutations from one-way functions
open: Determine whether arbitrary one-way functions imply efficiently evaluable, length-preserving one-way permutations.
status: Longstanding. Definitions involving keyed families and restricted domains require care; those variants do not automatically settle permutations on all bit strings.
why: This would clarify whether permutation structure is an additional cryptographic assumption.
key_works: Goldreich, 2005, *On One-Way Permutations: A Clarification*; Goldreich, Levin, and Nisan, 1995, *On Constructing 1-1 One-Way Functions*.

title: Goldreich-generator security against unrestricted efficient distinguishers
open: Prove suitable polynomial-stretch Goldreich local generators pseudorandom against all polynomial-time distinguishers, under a clearly stated, independently motivated assumption.
status: Since Goldreich’s local-function proposal. Concrete attacks and restricted-model analyses constrain predicates and stretch, but do not establish unrestricted security.
why: Local pseudorandomness would enable exceptionally cheap cryptographic computation.
key_works: Couteau, Dupin, Méaux, Rossi, and Rotella, 2018, *On the Concrete Security of Goldreich’s Pseudorandom Generator*, ePrint 2018/1162.

title: Classical polynomial-time integer factorization
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Find a classical randomized polynomial-time algorithm for factoring arbitrary integers, or establish meaningful lower bounds in a sufficiently expressive computational model.
status: Open for decades. Quantum polynomial-time algorithms do not resolve the classical problem.
why: This would transform computational number theory and invalidate factoring-based cryptography.
key_works: Boneh and Shoup, 2023, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*; Galbraith, 2012, *Mathematics of Public Key Cryptography*.

title: RSA inversion versus factoring
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Prove or refute that efficiently inverting RSA on random messages implies efficient factorization of the RSA modulus, without restricting the adversary to a generic algebraic model.
status: Open since RSA’s introduction. Generic-ring equivalence results do not establish unrestricted equivalence.
why: This would determine whether RSA rests on factoring hardness or a potentially weaker assumption.
key_works: Aggarwal and Maurer, 2009, *Breaking RSA Generically Is Equivalent to Factoring*.

title: Computational Diffie–Hellman versus discrete logarithms
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Establish general conditions under which solving computational Diffie–Hellman permits efficient discrete-logarithm computation, ideally covering cryptographically relevant prime-order groups without auxiliary smoothness assumptions.
status: Open in general. Reductions exist under additional group-order and number-theoretic conditions.
why: This would clarify the exact assumption underlying Diffie–Hellman protocols.
key_works: Maurer, 1994, *Towards the Equivalence of Breaking the Diffie-Hellman Protocol and Computing Discrete Logarithms*, DOI 10.1007/3-540-48658-5_26.

title: Non-generic attacks on ordinary prime-order elliptic curves
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Find an asymptotically sub-square-root classical discrete-logarithm algorithm for ordinary cryptographic elliptic curves without exploiting an already excluded special structure.
status: Open. Generic-group lower bounds do not exclude algorithms using the explicit curve representation.
why: This is a central unresolved security question for elliptic-curve cryptography.
key_works: Galbraith, 2012, *Mathematics of Public Key Cryptography*, elliptic-curve discrete logarithms.

title: Rigorous multivariate Coppersmith criteria
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Give efficiently checkable conditions guaranteeing that lattice-generated multivariate polynomial relations yield all intended small roots, without heuristic algebraic-independence assumptions.
status: Since the 1990s. Successful cryptanalytic applications coexist with gaps between lattice reduction and guaranteed root extraction.
why: This would distinguish proved attacks from experimentally successful heuristics.
key_works: Coppersmith, 1997, *Small Solutions to Polynomial Equations, and Low Exponent RSA Vulnerabilities*; Boneh–Durfee, 1999, *Cryptanalysis of RSA with Private Key \(d\) Less than \(N^{0.292}\)*.

title: Optimal RSA reconstruction thresholds from random leaked bits
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Determine sharp polynomial-time reconstruction thresholds when randomly positioned bits of specified RSA secret components are revealed, separating information-theoretic identifiability from algorithmic recovery.
status: Active since the 2000s. The 2009 reconstruction work exploits redundancy across RSA key components; thresholds depend strongly on which components leak.
why: This would quantify the damage caused by partial memory disclosure.
key_works: Heninger and Shacham, 2009, *Reconstructing RSA Private Keys from Random Key Bits*, ePrint 2008/510.

title: The \(d<N^{1/2}\) small-private-exponent RSA target
subfield: Classical public-key cryptanalysis and computational number theory
open: Determine whether balanced RSA with sufficiently small private exponent \(d<N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) can always be broken efficiently under appropriate standard parameter conditions.
status: Boneh–Durfee’s historical \(N^{0.292}\) milestone leaves a substantial gap to the \(N^{1/2}\) target.
why: This would settle a prominent boundary in RSA cryptanalysis.
key_works: Boneh and Durfee, 1999–2000, *Cryptanalysis of RSA with Private Key \(d\) Less than \(N^{0.292}\)*, DOI 10.1109/18.850673.

title: Fröberg’s conjecture for generic forms
open: Prove the predicted Hilbert series for ideals generated by generic homogeneous forms in the unresolved general parameter regimes.
status: Open since 1985. Numerous degrees, variable counts, and special cases are settled; the general conjecture is not.
why: It informs the algebraic regularity assumptions underlying polynomial-system complexity estimates.
key_works: Nenashev, 2017, *A Note on Fröberg’s Conjecture for Forms of Equal Degrees*, DOI 10.1016/j.crma.2017.01.011; Trung, arXiv:1803.04997.

title: Proving semi-regularity assumptions for random Boolean systems
open: Prove sharp high-probability algebraic regularity statements for random quadratic systems over \(\mathbb F_2\), sufficient to justify cryptanalytic solving-time estimates.
status: Algorithms with strong conditional bounds and supporting experiments exist; these are not unconditional typical-case analyses.
why: It would make multivariate security estimates mathematically firmer.
key_works: Bardet, Faugère, Salvy, and Spaenlehauer, 2013, *On the Complexity of Solving Quadratic Boolean Systems*, arXiv:1112.6263; DOI 10.1016/j.jco.2012.07.001.

title: Fully audited constant-time SQIsign signing
open: Deliver a complete signing implementation whose secret-dependent arithmetic, sampling, memory behavior, and exceptional paths satisfy a verified leakage model.
status: Constant-time four-dimensional lattice-reduction work addresses an important subroutine, not automatically the entire implementation.
why: Compact signatures are insufficient if signing leaks the private key.
key_works: Hanyecz et al., 2025, *Constant Time Lattice Reduction in Dimension 4 with Application to SQIsign*.

title: An eight-bit APN permutation
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Construct an almost-perfect-nonlinear permutation of \(\mathbb F_2^8\), or prove none exists.
status: The six-bit example does not extend the existence result to eight bits; major families and structural approaches have been excluded.
why: It would provide an optimal-differential permutation at the ubiquitous byte size.
key_works: Calderini, Sala, and Villa, 2017, *A Note on APN Permutations in Even Dimension*, DOI 10.1016/j.ffa.2017.02.001.

title: APN permutations in infinitely many even dimensions
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Construct an infinite family of APN permutations in even dimensions greater than six, or establish an obstruction ruling such families out.
status: Open. Generalized Kim-type constructions have substantial negative results rather than a general solution.
why: This would settle whether the six-bit phenomenon is exceptional.
key_works: Chase and Lisonek, 2020, *Kim-Type APN Functions Are Affine Equivalent to Gold Functions*, arXiv:2009.05937.

title: The exceptional APN conjecture
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Classify polynomials that remain APN over infinitely many extension fields, resolving the conjectured restriction to Gold and Kasami–Welch types up to the relevant equivalence.
status: The general problem remains; special degree families have been eliminated or classified. Recent special-case resolutions must not be mistaken for the full conjecture.
why: It would classify indefinitely extensible optimal differential constructions.
key_works: Aubry et al., 2022–2023, *Polynomials with Maximal Differential Uniformity and the Exceptional APN Conjecture*, arXiv:2207.13945.

title: Complete CCZ classification of quadratic eight-bit APN functions
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Enumerate all quadratic APN functions on eight bits up to CCZ equivalence, with machine-checkable completeness and inequivalence certificates.
status: Large collections of new examples exist, but a catalogue of examples is not a completeness proof.
why: A complete census would test structural conjectures and improve construction methods.
key_works: Beierle and Leander, 2021/2022, *New Instances of Quadratic APN Functions*, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 68, 670–678; Bergen Boolean-function tables.

title: An eight-bit APN function with only 21 non-bent components
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Construct an eight-bit quadratic APN function attaining the proposed extremal amplitude distribution, equivalently the specified 21 nontrivial non-bent components, or prove impossibility.
status: Explicit unresolved instance highlighted in Open Problem 6.1 of the cited 2026 revision.
why: It would decide whether a new geometric lower bound is attained.
key_works: Bénéteau et al., *On the Walsh Spectra of Quadratic APN Functions*, arXiv:2510.12008, §6.

title: Maximum Boolean nonlinearity in odd dimensions
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Determine the maximum nonlinearity of Boolean functions for unresolved odd numbers of variables, and its asymptotic behavior.
status: Longstanding; constructions and upper bounds do not coincide in general.
why: This determines optimal resistance to affine approximation.
key_works: Carlet, 2021, *Boolean Functions for Cryptography and Coding Theory*, DOI 10.1017/9781108606806, chapter “Open Questions.”

title: Asymptotic enumeration of bent functions
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Obtain matching asymptotic upper and lower bounds for the number of bent Boolean functions, ideally identifying the leading growth term.
status: Large explicit families and counting bounds exist, but general enumeration remains unresolved.
why: It would measure how much of the optimal-nonlinearity landscape known constructions cover.
key_works: Carlet, 2021, *Boolean Functions for Cryptography and Coding Theory*, DOI 10.1017/9781108606806.

title: A substantial single-key attack on full AES-128
open: Find a full-round, single-key AES-128 key-recovery attack with a substantial advantage over exhaustive search under explicitly bounded data and memory.
status: Biclique cryptanalysis gives a historical slight theoretical improvement, not a practical break.
why: It would reveal structure not captured by current security assessments.
key_works: Bogdanov, Khovratovich, and Rechberger, 2011, *Biclique Cryptanalysis of the Full AES*, ePrint 2011/449.

title: Full SHA-256 collisions below birthday complexity
open: Construct collisions for full, untruncated SHA-256 with total work substantially below the generic \(2^{128}\) scale.
status: Reduced-round and modified-initial-state results do not solve the standard-function problem.
why: Collision resistance underpins signatures, commitments, and content addressing.
key_works: NIST, 2015, *Secure Hash Standard*, FIPS 180-4.

title: Full SHA-256 preimages below generic search
open: Find preimages of independently specified SHA-256 outputs with a substantial classical advantage over generic \(2^{256}\)-scale search.
status: A distinct problem from collision finding; reduced-round preimage results do not settle it.
why: It tests a separate security property used by commitments and hash-based constructions.
key_works: NIST, 2015, *Secure Hash Standard*, FIPS 180-4.

title: Full SHA3-256 preimages below generic search
open: Recover a preimage of a specified full SHA3-256 digest with a substantial classical advantage over generic search.
status: Separate from collisions, distinguishers, and reduced-round permutation attacks.
why: Preimage security is a foundational assumption for many higher-level constructions.
key_works: NIST, 2015, FIPS 202.

title: Learned cryptanalysis that transfers to full-strength targets
open: Demonstrate a reproducible learned attack on a full-strength standardized primitive that beats the best matched non-learning attack after counting training, data, and inference.
status: Gohr’s 2019 work established important reduced-round results, not general full-round superiority.
why: It would determine whether machine learning adds cryptanalytic power rather than benchmark-specific speedups.
key_works: Gohr, 2019, *Improving Attacks on Round-Reduced Speck32/64 Using Deep Learning*, ePrint 2019/037.

title: Unbounded FHE from plain LWE
open: Construct fully homomorphic encryption supporting unbounded iterative computation from plain LWE without an additional circular-security assumption or a depth bound fixed at key generation.
status: Leveled FHE from LWE is established; that is not the same statement.
why: It would close a central assumption gap in general encrypted computation.
key_works: Brakerski–Vaikuntanathan, 2011/2014, *Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption from (Standard) LWE*; Micciancio–Vaikuntanathan, 2024, *SoK: Learning with Errors, Circular Security, and Fully Homomorphic Encryption*.

title: General encrypted inference within tenfold plaintext cost
open: Achieve at most 10× end-to-end cost for a declared, representative inference suite while preserving model utility, input privacy, and a fixed security level.
status: Proposed moonshot, not a claim that every specialized model lacks efficient private evaluation.
why: It would make confidential inference broadly deployable rather than task-specific.
key_works: Chillotti et al., *TFHE*, ePrint 2018/421; Jiang, Lou, and Joshi, 2022, *MATCHA*, arXiv:2202.08814.

title: Indistinguishability obfuscation from plain LWE
subfield: Obfuscation, functional encryption, and advanced access control
open: Construct indistinguishability obfuscation for general polynomial-size circuits from plain LWE without circular security or additional independent assumptions.
status: iO from combinations of well-founded assumptions is established; circular-secure LWE suffices in another line. Plain LWE remains the sharper target.
why: It would consolidate an exceptionally powerful primitive onto one major assumption.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai, 2020–2021, ePrint 2020/1003; Brakerski et al., 2020–2022, *Factoring and Pairings Are Not Necessary for iO*, ePrint 2020/1024.

title: Practical general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation
subfield: Obfuscation, functional encryption, and advanced access control
open: Obfuscate nontrivial general circuits with independently analyzed security and executable artifacts small and fast enough for ordinary machines.
status: Proposed moonshot; existence constructions do not constitute practical general-purpose software protection.
why: It would enable applications currently confined to theoretical feasibility.
key_works: Jain, Lin, and Sahai, 2020–2021, *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, ePrint 2020/1003.

title: Collusion-resistant general functional encryption from plain LWE
subfield: Obfuscation, functional encryption, and advanced access control
open: Construct public-key functional encryption for general circuits, secure against unbounded polynomially many colluding function keys, from plain LWE with useful compactness.
status: General functional encryption follows from stronger combinations of assumptions; that does not settle this single-assumption target.
why: It would support fine-grained computation on encrypted data.
key_works: Jain, Lin, and Sahai, 2020–2021, *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, ePrint 2020/1003.

title: Practical functional encryption beyond narrow algebraic functions
subfield: Obfuscation, functional encryption, and advanced access control
open: Implement general-circuit functional encryption with independently reviewed security and tractable key generation, ciphertext size, and decryption for substantial circuits.
status: Proposed engineering target; efficient special-purpose inner-product systems do not solve general-circuit practicality.
why: It would let data owners release computed answers without releasing the underlying data.
key_works: Garg et al., 2013, *Candidate Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption for All Circuits*, ePrint 2013/451.

title: Quantitative utility–leakage frontiers for searchable encryption
subfield: Private retrieval, oblivious memory, and encrypted databases
open: Characterize the minimum leakage necessary to achieve specified search costs, and translate leakage into adversarial reconstruction success under explicit auxiliary-information models.
status: Leakage-abuse attacks show that seemingly modest leakage can be highly revealing; universal quantitative frontiers remain absent.
why: This would make encrypted-search security comparable across designs.
key_works: Cash, Grubbs, Perry, and Ristenpart, 2015, *Leakage-Abuse Attacks Against Searchable Encryption*, DOI 10.1145/2810103.2813700.

title: Practical post-quantum verifiable delay functions
subfield: Signatures, threshold cryptography, and delay functions
open: Construct a VDF with credible post-quantum sequentiality, compact proofs, fast verification, and an explicit assumption weaker than simply assuming the whole desired primitive.
status: Classical unknown-order-group constructions are major milestones but do not establish post-quantum security.
why: It would support durable delay-based protocols after quantum migration.
key_works: Boneh, Bonneau, Bünz, and Fisch, 2018, *Verifiable Delay Functions*, ePrint 2018/601; Boneh et al., 2018, *A Survey of Two Verifiable Delay Functions*, ePrint 2018/712.

title: Constant-time security under dynamic voltage and frequency scaling
subfield: Implementation security, formal verification, and physical leakage
open: Develop enforceable leakage models and countermeasures that account for secret-dependent power affecting execution time through frequency scaling.
status: Hertzbleed demonstrated that constant instruction timing is not sufficient against this mechanism.
why: It challenges a central software-side-channel abstraction.
key_works: Wang, Paccagnella, He, Shacham, and Fletcher, 2022, *Hertzbleed: Turning Power Side-Channel Attacks into Remote Timing Attacks on x86*.

title: Low-cost post-quantum strong asymmetric PAKE
open: Match the deployment efficiency and strong server-compromise properties of mature asymmetric PAKE designs using post-quantum assumptions and explicit composable security.
status: Proposed practicality target. OPAQUE already addresses precomputation resistance; generic resistance to offline guessing after total server compromise is not assumed.
why: Password-based systems also need quantum migration.
key_works: Jarecki, Krawczyk, and Xu, 2018, *OPAQUE: An Asymmetric PAKE Protocol Secure Against Pre-Computation Attacks*, ePrint 2018/163.

title: Compact post-quantum anonymous credentials
subfield: Anonymous credentials, coercion resistance, and private accountability
open: Achieve selective disclosure, unlinkable presentation, and malicious-issuer security with post-quantum assumptions and mobile-friendly proof sizes.
status: Proposed practical target; efficient pairing-based credentials establish a classical baseline, not quantum resistance.
why: Identity systems need privacy-preserving migration rather than simply larger signatures.

title: Revocation without presentation linkability
subfield: Anonymous credentials, coercion resistance, and private accountability
open: Revoke credentials promptly while preventing revocation checks, witness updates, and issuer interactions from linking a holder’s presentations.
status: Accumulators and revocation mechanisms address portions of the problem; lifecycle metadata remains part of the target.
why: A privacy-preserving credential should remain private when it expires or is revoked.
key_works: Sonnino et al., *Coconut*, arXiv:1802.07344; Melara et al., *CONIKS*, ePrint 2014/1004.

title: Public-key quantum money from plain LWE in the standard model
open: Construct publicly verifiable quantum money from plain LWE with standard-model security, without generic-group-action or ideal-oracle qualifications.
status: Generic-model constructions from standard assumptions are substantial progress but do not settle this target.
why: It would ground reusable quantum tokens in a widely studied assumption.
key_works: Doliskani, 2025–2026, *Public-Key Quantum Money from Standard Assumptions (In the Generic Model)*, ePrint 2025/092.

title: Standard-model quantum-state obfuscation for useful restricted classes
open: Replace classical-oracle idealizations in quantum-state obfuscation by explicit constructions for useful restricted program classes under stated assumptions.
status: Oracle-model results for pseudodeterministic classical-input/output computation do not establish unrestricted standard-model obfuscation.
why: It would turn a powerful idealized primitive into a concrete one.
key_works: Bartusek, Brakerski, and Vaikuntanathan, 2024, *Quantum State Obfuscation from Classical Oracles*, arXiv:2401.10200.

title: Long-distance field device-independent QKD
open: Demonstrate positive finite-key device-independent secret-key generation over a declared long-distance field link without fair-sampling assumptions or hidden trusted measurement-device models.
status: Bell-certified experimental QKD was demonstrated in 2022; long-distance field operation is a stronger target.
why: It would move device-independent security toward deployable communication.
key_works: Nadlinger et al., 2022, *Experimental Quantum Key Distribution Certified by Bell’s Theorem*, DOI 10.1038/s41586-022-04941-5.

title: Exact secret-key capacity of thermal-loss channels
open: Determine the exact two-way assisted secret-key capacity of general bosonic thermal-loss channels by matching achievable rates with upper bounds.
status: The pure-loss repeaterless capacity is known; nonzero thermal noise leaves broader unresolved regimes.
why: It would establish fundamental limits for realistic optical communication.
key_works: Pirandola, Laurenza, Ottaviani, and Banchi, 2017, *Fundamental Limits of Repeaterless Quantum Communications*, DOI 10.1038/ncomms15043.

title: Secure memory-based repeater advantage in a complete field system
open: Demonstrate an end-to-end, finite-key-secure memory-based repeater chain exceeding the appropriate point-to-point benchmark while reporting all elementary-link and memory resources.
status: Proposed experimental target; changing the network model does not “violate” a repeaterless bound.
why: It would validate the practical value of quantum repeaters for cryptographic communication.
key_works: Pirandola et al., 2017, *Fundamental Limits of Repeaterless Quantum Communications*, arXiv:1510.08863.

title: Verifiable ordering guarantees with explicit economic meaning
subfield: Decentralized protocols and cryptographic economic systems
open: Connect formal ordering properties to bounded adversarial economic advantage under congestion and strategic submission, rather than assuming that one fairness definition eliminates all extractable value.
status: Proposed theory target; order fairness and economic fairness are not identical notions.
why: It would make cryptographic ordering guarantees meaningful for actual applications.
key_works: Kelkar et al., 2020, *Order-Fairness for Byzantine Consensus*; Kelkar et al., 2023, *Themis: Fast, Strong Order-Fairness in Byzantine Consensus*.

title: R11.01. Helleseth’s vanishing conjecture beyond established exponent families
open: Prove that, whenever \(q>2\) and \(d\equiv1\pmod{p-1}\), some nonzero \(a\) satisfies \(W_{F,d}(a)=0\), or produce a counterexample.
status: Proposed in 1971. Niho exponents are settled in every characteristic; the unrestricted conjecture remains unresolved in the reviewed literature.
why: It would establish a universal spectral constraint rather than another family-specific calculation.
key_works: Liem Nguyen, 2020/2022, *On Weil Sums, Conjectures of Helleseth, and Niho Exponents*, arXiv:2006.15726, Conjecture 1.2.
aliases: Helleseth vanishing conjecture; singularity conjecture for power permutations.

title: R11.02. Helleseth’s three-valued conjecture in characteristic at least five
open: For \(F=\mathbb F_{p^n}\) with \(n\) a power of two, prove that an invertible exponent cannot have an exactly three-valued Weil spectrum when \(p\ge5\).
status: The conjecture dates to 1971. Characteristics two and three are proved; those results do not settle the remaining characteristics.
why: It would exclude an entire class of exceptionally sparse correlation spectra.
key_works: Daniel J. Katz, 2018, *Weil Sums of Binomials: Properties, Applications, and Open Problems*, arXiv:1805.10452, Conjecture 10.6.

title: R11.03. Symmetry of every three-valued Weil spectrum
open: Prove that every three-valued spectrum of an invertible power function has the form \(\{0,A,-A\}\), or exhibit an asymmetric example.
status: Integrality, the occurrence of zero, and opposite signs of the other values are established. Equality of their magnitudes remains the stronger conjecture.
why: It would turn several separate spectral restrictions into a rigid classification principle.
key_works: Katz, 2018, *Weil Sums of Binomials: Properties, Applications, and Open Problems*, arXiv:1805.10452, Conjecture 10.5.

title: R11.05. Divisibility of the product of distinct nonzero spectral values
open: Characterize exponents for which \(q\) divides the product of the **distinct nonzero** values of \(W_{F,d}\), initially restricting to integral spectra.
status: Explicit Problem 3.7 in Katz–Langevin. Fourier identities motivate the question but do not establish the divisibility generally.
why: This could supply new arithmetic obstructions to proposed spectra.
key_works: Daniel J. Katz and Philippe Langevin, 2014/2015, *New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth*, arXiv:1412.8530.

title: R11.06. A four-valued analogue of Katz’s spectral-structure theorem
open: Determine which integrality, zero-occurrence, and exponent-congruence restrictions survive when a power permutation has exactly four spectral values.
status: Explicit Problem 3.6 in Katz–Langevin; no general resolution was located. Their three-valued theorem does not automatically extend.
why: It would organize four-valued examples by structural necessity rather than construction alone.
key_works: Katz and Langevin, 2014/2015, *New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth*, arXiv:1412.8530.

title: R11.07. The optimal resilience of two-round full-information coin flipping
open: Determine the largest adversarial coalition tolerable by two-round collective coin-flipping protocols when each participant broadcasts one bit per round.
status: The 2025 bounds leave a gap between constructions tolerating roughly \(n/[\log n\,\operatorname{poly}(\log\log n)]\) corruptions and attacks using \(O(n/\log\log n)\).
why: This isolates the value of one additional interaction round.
key_works: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Mohit Gurumukhani, Noam Ringach, and Rocco Servedio, 2025, *Lower Bounds for Leader Election and Collective Coin Flipping, Revisited*, arXiv:2504.01856, §7.

title: R11.08. Simultaneously biasing polynomially many Boolean outputs
open: For every \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^{n^{0.01}}\), can one coalition of \(O(n/\log n)\) coordinates, using **one common strategy**, force each of \(0.01n^{0.01}\) selected output bits toward a chosen value with probability at least \(0.99\)?
status: Explicit Question 7.1 in the 2025 paper. Allowing different adversarial behavior for different outputs gives a weaker, established result.
why: A positive answer would sharpen the preceding coin-flipping lower bounds.
key_works: Chattopadhyay et al., 2025, *Lower Bounds for Leader Election and Collective Coin Flipping, Revisited*, arXiv:2504.01856.

title: R11.10. Vanishing-bias quantum weak coin flipping in constant quantum space
open: Construct ordinary, zero-penalty quantum weak coin-flipping protocols with arbitrarily small bias while keeping the number of qubits bounded independently of the bias; alternatively, prove space must grow.
status: Arbitrarily small bias is achievable, but the cited constructions require growing space. The 2025 penalty-based approach does not settle the zero-penalty case.
why: This separates communication-round complexity from quantum-memory requirements.
key_works: Atul Singh Arora, Carl A. Miller, Mauro E. S. Morales, and Jamie Sikora, 2025, *Cheat-Penalised Quantum Weak Coin-Flipping*, arXiv:2510.03218.

title: R11.20. Constant-rate worst-case two-split-state codes for quantum messages
open: Construct constant-rate non-malleable encodings of arbitrary quantum messages against two independently acting tamperers who may share entanglement, with negligible error and protection of external reference entanglement.
status: The cited work achieves weaker worst-case rate and stronger average-case results. Average-case constant rate does not settle arbitrary-message security.
why: It would remove a major efficiency gap in quantum tamper resistance.
key_works: Naresh Goud Boddu, Vipul Goyal, Rahul Jain, and João Ribeiro, 2023/2024, *Split-State Non-Malleable Codes and Secret Sharing Schemes for Quantum Messages*, arXiv:2308.06466, §1.4.

title: R11.21. The missing two-out-of-three quantum non-malleable threshold scheme
open: Construct non-malleable quantum secret sharing in which any two of three shares reconstruct, one share reveals nothing, and the declared split-state tampering guarantee holds.
status: The cited construction covers the other no-cloning-compatible threshold regimes but explicitly leaves the two-out-of-three case unresolved.
why: This is the smallest threshold configuration combining useful redundancy with quantum reconstruction.
key_works: Boddu, Goyal, Jain, and Ribeiro, *Split-State Non-Malleable Codes and Secret Sharing Schemes for Quantum Messages*, arXiv:2308.06466, open problems.

title: R11.23. Bidirectional ratcheting under continual leakage and full compromise
open: Extend leakage-resilient ratcheted key exchange to asynchronous bidirectional communication, combining bounded continual leakage with clearly specified recovery after full state compromise. State exactly which uncompromised updates and randomness assumptions permit recovery.
status: Collins–Colombo–Schaeffler’s 2025 construction is unidirectional and distinguishes sender and receiver leakage guarantees. Ordinary post-compromise security does not imply continual-leakage resilience.
why: It would close a model mismatch between interactive conversations and one-way leakage-resilient channels.
key_works: Daniel Collins, Simone Colombo, and Sina Schaeffler, 2025, *Towards Leakage-Resilient Ratcheted Key Exchange*, ePrint 2025/332; DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-91823-0_6.

title: FHE runtime for compiled workloads at interpreted-language speed
open: Build an FHE toolchain that compiles ordinary programs (Rust/C subsets, SQL, ML inference graphs) to FHE executions running within ~10-100x of plaintext interpreted speed (not today's 10^3-10^6x), with automated parameter/scheme selection (BFV/BGV/CKKS/TFHE-per-op), batching, and bootstrapping amortized by the compiler. Current compilers (Concrete, EVA, HEaaN.mlir lines) leave orders of magnitude on the table.
status: Concrete (Zama) targets ML inference with TFHE/BFV — still ~10^3x+ for general code; CKKS pipelines for inference-only niches approach 10^2x for narrow model classes. General compiled-workload FHE at 10-100x: absent.
why: Encrypted computation as a drop-in for cloud workloads (private SaaS, medical/genomic analytics, ad measurement) becomes deployable at 10-100x; below that it's demos only.
key_works: Concrete compiler (Zama, github.com/zama-ai/concrete); EVA (arXiv:1912.03174); HEaaN/CKKS (Cheon et al., arXiv:1704.03530); TFHE (arXiv:1608.06905).
aliases: practical FHE compiler; encrypted compute runtime

title: iO from one-way functions
open: Construct indistinguishability obfuscation from nothing stronger than the existence of one-way functions — the minimal plausible assumption. Current candidate iO needs bilinear maps, LWE, or CRT-style multilinear maps with strong security assumptions.
status: iO achieved from LWE-based multilinear-map-like tools (Garg–Gentry–Halevi line, 2013+), then from well-founded LWE variants (Jain–Lin–Sahai 2021+); OWF-only remains open; no impossibility known.
why: The holy grail of cryptographic obfuscation: "den Boer's dream" — obfuscation as weakly assumed as hashing; unlocks virtual black-box-ish power for all of crypto.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai, "Distinguishing-Obfuscation from LWE" (arXiv:2010.13642); Garg et al. candidate multilinear maps (eprint 2012/610); Sahai–Waters 2014 (eprint 2013/451) (verify).

title: Sound multilinear maps
open: Construct multilinear maps that resist zeroizing/averaging/nucleation attacks while supporting degree ≥ 3, with a plausible concrete-security story. All proposed maps (GGH13, CLT13, GGH15) have suffered decisive structural attacks; no current map family is considered sound.
status: GGH13 zeroizing (Cheon et al. 2015), CLT13 attacks (2020 CH ePrint line), GGH15 nucleation (Miles–Sahai–Zhandry 2016) (verify); the field awaits a surviving construction.
why: Multilinear maps were the path to general obfuscation, program obfuscation applications, and constrained PRFs; their collapse is the biggest open wound in crypto construction.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi (eprint 2012/610); Coron–Lepoint–Tibouchi (2013); Cheon et al. zeroizing (Eurocrypt 2015).

title: Transparent SNARK with constant proofs and linear-time proving
open: A zk-SNARK achieving simultaneously: transparent setup (no ceremony), O(1) proof size, prover time O(n) with small constants, and post-quantum security. STARKs give transparency+PQ but polylog proofs and quasilinear provers with heavy constants; pairing SNARKs give tiny proofs but trusted setup and non-PQ.
status: Each pair achievable; all four simultaneously: open. Folding schemes (Nova-style) move toward it via recursion but inherit hash-based prover costs.
why: The "everything SNARK": verification cheap enough for blockchains and browsers, no trust ceremony, quantum-safe.
key_works: Ben-Sasson et al. STARK (2018); Nova (arXiv:2111.12460); Bünz et al. transparent setups line (eprint 2018/646) (verify).

title: zkVM proving LLM inference
open: Prove correct execution of a full transformer forward pass (billions of FLOPs, gigabytes of weights) inside a zkVM with total proving cost under ~$0.01 per million tokens — currently 10^4-10^6x native cost, making per-token proving economically absurd. Needs: fixed-point numerics matching GPU nondeterminism bounds, attention as lookup-friendly circuits, weight-commitment reuse across queries.
status: zkML lines (ezkl, modulus, zkLLM paper arXiv:2404.16109) prove small nets (CNNs, toy transformers); frontier LLM inference unproven at any cost; no impossibility.
why: Verifiable AI: model-card enforcement, auditable API claims ("this output came from this weights hash"), anti-fraud in AI marketplaces, scientific reproducibility of model results.
key_works: zkLLM (arXiv:2404.16109); ezkl (github.com/zkonduit/ezkl); Mystic/Morphism lines (verify).

title: Verifiable training and fine-tuning
open: Produce succinct, publicly verifiable proofs that a model was trained on a claimed dataset/compute budget (with stated hyperparameters), hiding data contents — verifiable training via proof-carrying checkpoints, SNARK-friendly training logs, or GGM-style intermediate attestations. Open at every scale above toy models.
status: Proof-carrying data lines (BTC-style inscription attestations), zkML training experiments on MNIST-scale; full pretraining verification: no approach comes within orders of magnitude; no impossibility known.
why: Regulatory and scientific claims about training data/compute (provenance, licensing, "no PII", compliance) become checkable instead of self-attested.
key_works: Abadi et al. proof-carrying data (2015, verify); zkML training demos; Jolt/SP1 zkVM benchmarks.

title: Witness encryption for all of NP from standard assumptions
open: Construct witness encryption for arbitrary NP statements from standard assumptions (LWE, or even one-way functions). Current constructions need iO (WE follows from iO) or broken multilinear maps; Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters gave the first candidate from multilinear maps (2010), and no standard-assumption construction is known for all NP.
status: WE from iO: known. From snARGs for NP in CRS form: known (Choudhuri et al., Garg–Srinivasan lines, 2017+). From LWE directly: only for specific languages (graph isomorphism, some lattice-y statements). The general standard-assumption case: open — one of the cleanest big questions in the area.
why: WE is "encryption to a condition": the public key IS a puzzle. It converts proof-of-statement into decryption capability — the primitive underneath trustless bounties, dead-man switches, and conditional coordination.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters, "Candidate Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption for all circuits", FOCS 2013 + WE paper CRYPTO 2010; Choudhuri–Jain–Jin, "Non-Zero Sum..." (verify); Zhandry 2024 quantum WE (verify).

title: Infinite quadratic APN families with non-classical Walsh spectra
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Construct an infinite family of quadratic APN functions whose Walsh spectra are non-classical, rather than isolated finite-dimensional examples.
status: Explicitly identified as a major remaining question in the 2026 revision of the cited work.
why: It would reveal structural diversity beyond the dominant known families.
key_works: Bénéteau, Goluboff, Kölsch, and Vaghasiya, 2025–2026, *On the Walsh Spectra of Quadratic APN Functions*, arXiv:2510.12008.

title: Sharp bounds on bent components of quadratic APN functions
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Determine the maximum number of bent component functions of a quadratic APN map in each even dimension, with matching constructions or stronger impossibility bounds.
status: New nontrivial bounds appeared in the 2025–2026 work; sharpness remains unresolved in important regimes.
why: This links optimal differential behavior to linear-cryptanalysis resistance.
key_works: Bénéteau et al., 2025–2026, *On the Walsh Spectra of Quadratic APN Functions*, Open Problem 6.2, arXiv:2510.12008.

title: Sharp resilience–degree–nonlinearity tradeoffs
subfield: Boolean functions, S-boxes, and finite geometry
open: Determine the best attainable nonlinearity at prescribed variable count, correlation-immunity order, balance, and algebraic degree.
status: Classical inequalities constrain the region, but many parameter combinations lack matching constructions.
why: These tradeoffs govern robust combining and filtering functions.
key_works: Carlet, 2021, *Boolean Functions for Cryptography and Coding Theory*, chapter “Open Questions.”

title: Embedded SQIsign verification with a tenfold resource reduction
open: Reduce total verification energy or latency tenfold relative to a pinned optimized embedded implementation, preserving parameters and counting memory and preprocessing.
status: Proposed moonshot; optimized Intel and Cortex-M4 verification provides a concrete 2025 baseline.
why: It would make compact post-quantum signatures more attractive on constrained devices.
key_works: Aardal et al., 2025, *Optimized One-Dimensional SQIsign Verification on Intel and Cortex-M4*, DOI 10.46586/tches.v2025.i1.497-522.

title: Consensus with throughput-decentralization-latency all at once
open: Design a consensus protocol simultaneously achieving: >=100k TPS sustained, >=10k independent validators (no committee assumptions), <=1s finality on a WAN, and accountability (identifiable equivocation). Existing designs sit on a frontier: committees (high TPS, weak decentralization), fully-participatory DAG/BFT (decentralization, lower TPS), and no construction credibly claims all four; matching lower bounds are not known for the combined regime.
status: Hotstuff descendants + DAG-Metropolis/Narwhal-style decoupling push TPS with committees; Ethereum L1 keeps decentralization at ~10^2-10^3 TPS; Solana-style pushes latency+TPS at committee-ish hardware assumptions. Combined-envelope design open.
why: The throughput wall is the stated blocker for global-scale settlement; every major chain is a point on this frontier rather than beyond it.
key_works: Yin et al., "HotStuff", PODC 2019; Danezis et al., "Narwhal and Bullshark", SOSP 2022 (arXiv:2101.11927); Lewis-Pye et al. on DAG consensus (verify).
aliases: consensus design trilemma+; DAG BFT at global scale

title: Unconditional existence of one-way functions
open: Prove that a polynomial-time computable function family is hard to invert on a non-negligible fraction of randomly generated inputs, without assuming another computational hardness conjecture.
status: Foundational since the 1970s. Numerous candidates exist, but unconditional computational security remains unproved.
why: This would establish the foundations of computational cryptography rather than merely conditional constructions.
key_works: Boneh and Shoup, 2023, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*; MIT, 2025, *Open Questions* lecture.

title: Oblivious transfer from arbitrary public-key encryption
open: Determine whether the existence of arbitrary semantically secure public-key encryption implies oblivious transfer, without extra algebraic or structural assumptions.
status: Longstanding. Non-black-box developments do not provide a generic construction from every public-key encryption scheme.
why: Oblivious transfer supplies the foundation for general secure two-party computation.
key_works: Gertner, Kannan, Malkin, Reingold, and Viswanathan, 2000, *The Relationship Between Public Key Encryption and Oblivious Transfer*; Barnum–Heath, 2026, ePrint 2026/113.

title: Verifiable FHE with near-native evaluation cost
open: Prove correct encrypted execution against a malicious evaluator with less than 10% additional end-to-end cost on a declared workload suite.
status: Proposed moonshot; generic proof-system composition establishes feasibility, not this overhead target.
why: Confidentiality does not ensure an outsourced computation was performed correctly.
key_works: Ben-Sasson et al., 2018, *Scalable, Transparent, and Post-Quantum Secure Computational Integrity*, ePrint 2018/046; Chillotti et al., *TFHE*.

title: General two-party secret-key capacity
subfield: Information-theoretic secrecy, randomness, and tamper resistance
open: Determine the exact asymptotic secret-key rate obtainable from an arbitrary finite joint distribution of two honest parties’ observations and an eavesdropper’s information.
status: General lower and upper bounds exist; the July 2026 existence result for bipartite bound information does not supply a complete capacity formula.
why: It would characterize the secrecy inherently present in correlated data.
key_works: Maurer, 1993, DOI 10.1109/18.256484; Maurer–Wolf, 1999, *Intrinsic Conditional Information*; Pauwels–Gisin–Renner, 2026, arXiv:2607.25838.

title: Deciding positive distillable secrecy
subfield: Information-theoretic secrecy, randomness, and tamper resistance
open: Give a general effective criterion for whether a finite rational distribution has positive two-party distillable secret key under unrestricted public discussion.
status: Bound information now exists, so positive secrecy-formation cost alone cannot be used as the criterion.
why: A decision criterion would separate useful correlations from nondistillable secrecy.
key_works: Pauwels, Gisin, and Renner, 2026, *Bipartite Bound Information Exists*, arXiv:2607.25838.

title: Explicit two-split-state non-malleable codes approaching capacity
subfield: Information-theoretic secrecy, randomness, and tamper resistance
open: Construct efficient information-theoretic two-split-state non-malleable codes with rate approaching \(1/2\) and negligible error.
status: Capacity \(1/2\) is known; explicit rate-one-third constructions are an important milestone. Computational and extra-state results are different settings.
why: It would close a major explicit-construction gap in tamper resistance.
key_works: Cheraghchi–Guruswami, 2013–2014, *Capacity of Non-Malleable Codes*, arXiv:1309.0458; Aggarwal et al., 2022, *Rate One-Third Non-malleable Codes*.

title: Witness encryption from plain LWE
subfield: Obfuscation, functional encryption, and advanced access control
open: Construct witness encryption for general NP statements from plain LWE, without routing through stronger obfuscation assumptions.
status: General witness-encryption feasibility under stronger assumptions does not establish this target.
why: It would support encryption controlled by publicly specified computational witnesses.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai, 2020–2021, ePrint 2020/1003; Wu, 2026, *Lattice Assumptions with Hints*.

title: Composition of strong unclonability definitions
open: Determine which unclonable-encryption guarantees survive adaptive multi-instance use, entangled side information, and later key revelation, with tight implications or separations between definitions.
status: One-out-of-many constructions exist; their existence does not establish every stronger composition property.
why: Real applications use many correlated tokens or ciphertexts rather than one isolated challenge.
key_works: *One-out-of-Many Unclonable Cryptography: Definitions, Constructions, and More*, 2023–2026, arXiv:2302.09836; authors verify.

title: R11.17. Closing the machine-checked koalaIRS12 soundness interval
open: Narrow the gap between proved soundness and explicit attacks for the fixed **koalaIRS12** benchmark, with contributions checked by its Lean formalization. Determine the optimum within the pinned model, rather than changing the protocol or threat model.
status: On 6 October 2026, the challenge reports an interval of **68.15 to 116.13 security bits**. The upper endpoint already excludes a 128-bit claim for this benchmark.
why: It provides a measurable target where either a stronger proof or a better attack is valuable.
key_works: Ethereum Foundation Formal Verification Team, 2026, *Raising Machine-Checked Security Benchmarks to Advance Hash-Based SNARKs through Agentic Collaboration*; the live better.codes benchmark and accepted certificates.

title: R11.09. Perfectly fair leader election beyond commit-and-reveal lower bounds
open: Determine whether the logarithmic-round barrier for perfect game-theoretic fairness extends beyond commit-and-reveal-style protocols. In particular, preserve each honest participant’s election probability of at least \(1/n\) against \(n^\varepsilon\)-sized coalitions, using the same abort and fairness definitions.
status: The TCC 2024 work proves an \(\Omega(\log n)\) lower bound for the restricted protocol class. Sublogarithmic protocols with both approximate fairness and weaker coalition requirements do not answer this question.
why: It would distinguish a fundamental fairness barrier from a limitation of a familiar protocol architecture.
key_works: Ohad Klein, Ilan Komargodski, and Chenzhi Zhu, 2024/2025, *On the (Im)possibility of Game-Theoretically Fair Leader Election Protocols*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-78011-0_13.

title: R11.11. A rigorous constant-space family for finite-penalty quantum coin flipping
open: For a fixed finite cheating penalty, prove a constant-qubit protocol family whose maximum dishonest expected payoff approaches \(1/2\). A concrete target is 24 qubits with penalty \(\Lambda=0.01\).
status: The 2025 paper supplies low-bias numerical constructions and evidence for arbitrarily small bias; finite examples are not a proof for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
why: It would turn numerical point-game evidence into an asymptotic resource theorem.
key_works: Arora, Miller, Morales, and Sikora, 2025, *Cheat-Penalised Quantum Weak Coin-Flipping*, arXiv:2510.03218.

title: R11.19. Bit-polynomial-time decoding behind the new capacity theorem
open: For fixed slack from capacity, replace the new decoder’s \(q^{O_\gamma(1)}\) dependence by running time polynomial in \(n\) and \(\log q\), while retaining its decoding radius and complete output list.
status: The September 2026 preprint gives polynomial dependence on field cardinality, not its bit length. This distinction matters when \(q\) is very large.
why: It separates an algorithmic existence theorem from scalability over cryptographic-size fields.
key_works: Jeronimo, 2026, *Algorithmic List Decoding at Capacity and Optimal Proximity Gaps for Reed–Solomon Codes*, arXiv:2609.05870.

title: R11.22. Hardware-free stateful leakage resilience against NC¹
open: Eliminate trusted hardware from the stateful leakage-resilient-circuit setting studied by Wang, while retaining its bounded-complexity leakage guarantee; alternatively, prove a broader impossibility under the same model.
status: The July 2026 revision obtains a trusted component whose size is independent of the original circuit. It also blocks a proposed hardware-elimination route through the simultaneous requirements of perfect soundness and verifiable CRS generation; this does not exclude every alternative route.
why: It would determine whether the remaining trusted component is essential.
key_works: Yuyu Wang, 2025–2026, *Leakage-Resilient Circuits against NC¹, Revisited*, ePrint 2025/1463.

title: R11.28. Plain-LWE receiver-non-committing IBE over an unrestricted identity space
open: Construct receiver-non-committing identity-based encryption from plain LWE for exponentially many possible identities, with polynomial-size public parameters and the full adaptive-exposure security required by the cited definition.
status: The February 2026 paper obtains DDH/LWE constructions for a polynomial-size identity space with compact public parameters. Its stronger pairing-based constructions do not remove this restriction under plain LWE.
why: It would support adaptive simulation without fixing a small universe of users in advance.
key_works: Rishab Goyal, Fuyuki Kitagawa, Venkata Koppula, Mahesh Sreekumar Rajasree, Ryo Nishimaki, and Takashi Yamakawa, 2026, *Non-Committing Attribute and Identity Based Encryption: Constructions and Applications*, author-hosted manuscript.

title: Superpolynomial lower bounds for unrestricted secret sharing
subfield: Secret sharing, secure computation, and correlated randomness
open: Prove superpolynomial worst-case share-size lower bounds for general, potentially nonlinear, perfect secret-sharing schemes.
status: The worst-case **linear** exponent gap was resolved in 2026; unrestricted nonlinear lower bounds remain a different problem.
why: It would establish fundamental limits on implementing arbitrary access policies.
key_works: Nir, 2026, *Resolving the Worst-Case Complexity of Linear Secret Sharing*, ECCC TR26-146.

title: Near-zero active-security overhead for large MPC workloads
subfield: Secret sharing, secure computation, and correlated randomness
open: Bring actively secure computation within 10% of a matched semi-honest implementation across a declared workload suite, counting preprocessing and failed executions.
status: Proposed moonshot; extensive protocol engineering has reduced costs but does not establish a universal small-overhead result.
why: Deployments should not have to trade away malicious-adversary protection.
key_works: Keller, 2020, *MP-SPDZ: A Versatile Framework for Multi-Party Computation*, DOI 10.1145/3372297.3417872.

title: Full ChaCha20 cryptanalysis below generic key search
open: Find a valid full-round ChaCha20 key-recovery or distinguishing attack beating the corresponding generic bound under realistic data limits.
status: Research attacks continue to target much smaller round counts; those results are not full-ChaCha20 breaks.
why: ChaCha’s deployment makes its remaining security margin consequential.
key_works: Wang et al., 2026, *Enhanced Differential-Linear Cryptanalysis of ChaCha Based on Bit Puncturing*, ePrint 2026/1837.

title: Verifiable computation on encrypted data (FHE × ZK)
open: Combine FHE and ZK so a cloud server proves IN ZERO KNOWLEDGE that it correctly evaluated the circuit on ciphertexts it cannot decrypt — verifiable FHE where the proof hides nothing beyond correctness. Current VC-over-FHE (PINNs, GIPs) adds significant overhead; the design target is overhead within 10x of plain FHE.
status: Gentry–Wichs impossibility separates proof-of-correctness from information-theoretic checking, but succinct ZK proofs over homomorphic ciphertexts exist at overhead; the practical combined runtime: open target.
why: The full stack of delegated encrypted compute: confidentiality (FHE) + integrity (ZK) + succinctness — "don't trust the cloud at all."
key_works: Gennaro–Gentry–Parno verifiable computation (2010); Gentry–Wichs (STOC 2011); FHE+SNARK hybrid lines (verify).

title: Low-memory proving for very large computations
subfield: Zero knowledge, succinct arguments, and recursive proofs
open: Prove a declared hundred-million-step workload within a one-gigabyte working-memory budget and less than twice the time of an unrestricted-memory baseline.
status: Proposed target; streaming, recursion, and recomputation techniques address different parts of the tradeoff.
why: It would broaden proving beyond high-memory servers.
key_works: Kothapalli and Setty, 2023, *HyperNova: Recursive Arguments for Customizable Constraint Systems*, ePrint 2023/573.
